chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, when I completed the rites of my 'umrah, I went to my wife before cutting my hair short. He said: A camel is due from you. He said: I said: When I wanted that from her and she had not yet cut her hair short, she refused; then when I overpowered her, she bit off some of her hair with her teeth. He said: May Allah have mercy on her; she was more knowledgeable than you. A camel is due from you, and there is nothing upon her.

key_terms.أُقَصِّرْ: to perform taqsir, shortening the hair to exit ihram
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهَا شَيْءٌ: no liability or expiation is due upon her

ai.seo_question: If someone has intercourse before taqsir after 'umrah al-tamattu', what expiation is required?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who has not yet fully exited the ihram of tamattu' by performing taqsir after 'umrah, yet has intercourse with his wife. The Imam عليه السلام rules that a badanah is obligatory upon the man, while the woman bears no liability in this case because she acted with awareness and initially refused.
